title: For a complex semisimple g and nonroot-of-unity q, a tensor product of two irreducible highest-weight U_q(g)-modules with an infinite-dimensional factor is completely reducible exactly when the product contravariant form is nondegenerate on its singular vectors
author: Andrey I. Mudrov
work: Contravariant Form on Tensor Product of Highest Weight Modules
source_version: Official SIGMA 15 (2019) article 026, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2019.026; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

source_locator.theorem: Theorem 6.3, quantum case with at least one infinite-dimensional factor
source_locator.label: dir-sum

difficulty_reason: The difficult direction must show that nondegeneracy on singular vectors exhausts the entire possibly infinite-dimensional tensor product, not merely that its visible highest-weight submodules split. The author constructs reciprocal extremal spaces and a twist operator, identifies its form with the tensor Shapovalov restriction, and proves both exhaustion and irreducibility by height induction. This addresses a genuine infinite-dimensional representation-theory problem beyond the finite-dimensional Weyl theorem.

source_check.note: The full original Theorem 6.3 and complete author proof are retained; the selected quantum case with an infinite-dimensional factor is specified on the cover. Standard quantum-group/Shapovalov facts remain author-cited prerequisites. Classical and finite-dimensional consequences are not additional counted problems. proof_review.note: The complete quantum-case Theorem6.3 proof and new Sections3–6 constructions were read. The author parametrizes singular vectors by reciprocal extremal subspaces, explicitly defines the twist map and its canonical-form pullback, then develops a height filtration: surjectivity exhausts the full tensor product by highest-weight submodules, and injectivity makes those submodules irreducible. The coevaluation lift and independence from its choice are explicitly supplied. Standard Shapovalov-form and quantum-group facts are background; the proof does not invoke finite-dimensional Weyl reducibility to cover infinite factors. Select the quantum case with at least one infinite-dimensional irreducible factor; neither the classical limit nor finite-dimensional unitarity corollaries are counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly the quantum branch of Theorem6.3: g finite-dimensional complex semisimple, U_q(g) with the stated triangular decomposition and coproduct, q nonzero and not a root of unity; V,Z irreducible highest-weight modules, with at least one infinite-dimensional. The canonical symmetric contravariant form is the product of the factor Shapovalov forms, contravariant for omega=antipode^{-1} composed with sigma, and (V tensor Z)^+ is the space annihilated by every positive Chevalley generator. Complete reducibility holds iff its restriction to that space is nondegenerate. Neither a finite-dimensional Weyl theorem nor a classical q->1 limiting proof is selected.
